info.name: Carrivo API
info.description:
REST API for **Carrivo**, a courier & logistics platform (customers ship and pay, couriers pick up and deliver, admins run hubs, zones, pricing, users and reports).

## How to use
1. **Set `baseUrl`** (collection variables): `http://localhost:5000/api/v1` locally, or `https://<your-api>.vercel.app/api/v1` for the live API.
2. **Set `demoPassword`** to the demo password you were given (it is empty here on purpose; the collection never stores real passwords or tokens).
3. **Run Auth → `Login as Admin (private credentials)`, `Login as Admin Viewer (demo, read-only)`, `Login as Courier (demo)`, `Login as Customer (demo)`.** Each saves its token into `adminToken`, `viewerToken`, `courierToken` or `customerToken` automatically, and every request already uses the right one (Authorization: Bearer).
4. Explore the module folders in order: Zones → Hubs → Pricing → Shipments (create, pickup, assign, status flow, proof) → Tracking → Payments → Couriers → Admin → Notifications. Requests that create something save its id (`shipmentId`, `paymentId`, ...) for the next requests.
5. **RBAC matrix**: run the folder (Runner) after logging in. Every request must be refused (401 / 403 / 404), except the viewer's reads (200) and has a test asserting the exact status; none of them can change data (forbidden-write probes carry an invalid body as a second safety net).

**Response envelope**: success `{ success: true, message, data, meta? }` (meta = `{ page, limit, total, totalPages }` on lists); error `{ success: false, message, errors: [] }`.
**Lists** accept `page`, `limit` (max 100), `sortBy`, `sortOrder`, `searchTerm` and module filters (see each request's disabled query params).
**Money** is a decimal string in USD (e.g. `"6.00"`). **Weights** are pounds (`weightLb`); **addresses** are US format (`street, City, ST 12345`); **phones** are US numbers; dates are business days in America/New_York.

Payments use Stripe **test mode** (card 4242 4242 4242 4242). Uploads (proof of delivery) are multipart, ≤ 4 MB; the frontend should compress photos first.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Email/password auth (Better Auth + bearer plugin). Send the returned `data.token` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
Rate limits (shared across instances via Redis): login, register and change-password allow 20 FAILED attempts per 15 min per IP.
Only these Better Auth endpoints are reachable: get-session, change-password, revoke-sessions, revoke-other-sessions, ok.
Everything else under /auth (e.g. list-sessions, verify-password, social sign-in) returns our 404 envelope.

item.name: Google: start sign-in (open in a BROWSER)

request.description:
Not an XHR call: the frontend NAVIGATES the browser here (window.location). Answers 302 to Google and sets two httpOnly cookies on the API domain (Better Auth's OAuth state + the signed challenge).
After Google, the browser ends on FRONTEND_URL/auth/google/callback?code=<one-time code> or ?error=account_exists | account_deactivated | google_cancelled | google_failed.
account_exists: the email already has an account (Google never links to it; use the password).

Manual test without a frontend (also in README → Authentication):
VERIFIER=$(openssl rand -base64 48 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=\n')
CHALLENGE=$(printf '%s' "$VERIFIER" | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | openssl base64 -A | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=')
Put both into the googleCodeVerifier / googleChallenge collection variables, open {{baseUrl}}/auth/google?challenge=<CHALLENGE> in a browser, sign in, copy ?code= from the address bar into googleCode, then send "Google: exchange code" within 60 s.

item.description:
Price (USD, the platform currency) = baseFee + ceil(max(0, weight - baseWeightLb)) × perLbFee, i.e. extra weight is charged per started pound.
Rule lookup: active rule for (serviceType, originZone, destinationZone), else the service's default rule (both zones null).
No rule → 422. Weight above the rule's maxWeightLb → 422. Money fields are strings (Decimal).

item.name: Shipments
item.description:
All routes need a Bearer token. Scope: CUSTOMER sees own shipments, COURIER sees assigned ones, ADMIN sees all.
Shipments outside your scope return 404 (not 403) so ids can't be probed.
Price is always calculated on the server; sending price/status/trackingId returns 400.
Workflow: pickup (customer) → assign (admin) → PATCH /status (courier/admin, see each request) → DELIVERED or RETURNED.

item.description:
A CUSTOMER applies to become a COURIER; an ADMIN approves or rejects (ADMIN_VIEWER reads only).

- One PENDING application per user (a partial unique index backs it); after a rejection, apply again after 7 days (the 409 names the date).
- No driver licence, SSN or other government ID is collected: unknown body fields are refused (400).
- Approve runs in one transaction (same path as an admin role change): courier profile from the application, role COURIER, every session of the applicant revoked (their old token gets 401; signing in again gives a COURIER token). A repeat decision gets 409 with the current status.
- Run order: `Apply` (customer, saves courierApplicationId) → `My applications` → staff `List`/`Get` → `Approve` or `Reject`. In a local/dev seed, applicant1@carrivo.dev and applicant2@carrivo.dev (demo password) have PENDING applications that can be approved; customer1 owns unfinished demo shipments, so approving one of theirs returns 409 with the unfinished count.

request.description:
CUSTOMER only. Body: phone (US), vehicleType (BICYCLE | MOTORCYCLE | CAR | VAN | TRUCK), availability (WEEKDAYS | WEEKENDS | FULL_TIME), preferredZoneId? | null, vehiclePlate? | null, experience? (≤ 500), about? (≤ 1000).
ADMIN → 403, ADMIN_VIEWER → 403 read-only, COURIER → 409 (all before validation). 409 when a PENDING one exists or the 7-day wait after a rejection runs. Rate limit: 10 submits/cancels per hour per user.
